items.explanation: Trump withdrew from Obama's 2015 Iran nuclear deal in 2018, calling it too weak — one of his signature reversals of Obama-era foreign policy.
items.stem: The Obama foreign-policy initiative Trump vowed to overturn was

option_explanations.A: The Affordable Care Act was a domestic health-care law, not a foreign-policy initiative. Trump opposed it, but the question asks for a foreign-policy initiative.
option_explanations.B: Border wall construction was Trump's own initiative, not Obama's. It cannot be the Obama policy he vowed to overturn.
option_explanations.C: Correct. Trump withdrew from Obama's 2015 Iran nuclear deal (JCPOA) in 2018, calling it too weak — one of his signature reversals of Obama-era foreign policy.
option_explanations.D: The USA Patriot Act was George W. Bush's 2001 law, not Obama's. It was not the Obama foreign-policy initiative in question.

items.explanation: Democrats charged the Trump campaign with colluding with Russia — the subject of the FBI's Crossfire Hurricane probe and the Mueller investigation.
items.stem: Trump's campaign was accused of colluding with

option_explanations.A: Correct. Democrats charged the Trump campaign with colluding with Russia — the subject of the FBI's Crossfire Hurricane probe and the Mueller investigation.
option_explanations.B: China was not the country the Trump campaign was accused of colluding with. The collusion charges centered on Russia, not China.
option_explanations.C: France was not the country in question — the collusion allegations involved Russia, not France.
option_explanations.D: North Korea was not the country in question — Trump's dealings with North Korea were a separate diplomatic story, not the collusion charge.

items.explanation: After Russia invaded Ukraine in 2022, Biden rallied NATO and sent billions in military and diplomatic aid to Kyiv.
items.stem: President Biden gave military and diplomatic support to

option_explanations.A: Biden did not give military and diplomatic support to Iraq in this period — the Iraq war era was over, and the question's answer is Ukraine.
option_explanations.B: Correct. After Russia invaded Ukraine in 2022, Biden rallied NATO and sent billions in military and diplomatic aid to Kyiv.
option_explanations.C: Biden did not support Afghanistan — he withdrew American forces from Afghanistan in 2021, ending the war there. The aid flowed to Ukraine.
option_explanations.D: Biden did not support Russia — Russia was the invader. American support went to Ukraine, against Russia.

items.explanation: Like Jackson, Trump ran as the outsider champion of 'the people' against a corrupt establishment — populist, anti-elite, and personally combative.
items.stem: Trump's populism and attacks on the establishment most resemble

option_explanations.A: George Washington was the opposite of a populist outsider — he was the consensus founding figure, unanimously elected. His style bears no resemblance to Trump's populism.
option_explanations.B: Abraham Lincoln was not a populist outsider attacking the establishment — he was a party politician who led the nation through civil war. The comparison does not fit.
option_explanations.C: Thomas Jefferson was an elite Virginia planter and philosopher-president, not an outsider populist railing against a corrupt establishment. The style is different.
option_explanations.D: Correct. Like Jackson, Trump ran as the outsider champion of 'the people' against a corrupt establishment — populist, anti-elite, and personally combative.

items.explanation: COVID-19's global death toll and social disruption most closely parallel the 1918 influenza pandemic, which killed over 600,000 Americans.
items.stem: The COVID-19 pandemic most closely resembles

option_explanations.A: The Great Depression was an economic collapse, not a pandemic. COVID-19 was a disease crisis; the comparison is to another pandemic, not an economic one.
option_explanations.B: Correct. COVID-19's global death toll and social disruption most closely parallel the 1918 influenza pandemic, which killed over 600,000 Americans.
option_explanations.C: The Red Scare was a political panic about communism, not a pandemic. It has nothing in common with a viral outbreak.
option_explanations.D: The First Great Awakening was an 18th-century religious revival, not a pandemic. It belongs to an entirely different story.

items.explanation: Trump frames the struggle as a shared moral cause: 'a coalition of nations who share the aim of stamping out extremism,' 'our shared resolve and our mutual respect,' a future 'that does honor to God.' He is recruiting Muslim-majority nations as partners against extremism -- the opposite of a war on Islam, a unilateral crusade, or an America-only fight.
options: A. A war of America against Islam
B. A shared battle of good against evil uniting all faiths
C. A purely military operation with no diplomacy
D. A conflict only the United States can fight
items.stem: In the speech, Trump frames the fight against extremism as
items.stimulus:
Questions 6–8 refer to the following excerpt (paraphrased).

In his 2017 address in Riyadh, President Trump pledged to strengthen old friendships and build new partnerships — urging Arab and Muslim leaders to join the United States in confronting Islamist extremism and isolating Iran.
—After President Donald Trump's speech in Saudi Arabia, May 2017

option_explanations.A: Trump explicitly framed the fight as NOT a war against Islam — he was addressing Muslim leaders as partners. A war of America against Islam is the opposite of his framing.
option_explanations.B: Correct. Trump frames the struggle as a shared moral cause: 'a coalition of nations who share the aim of stamping out extremism' — a battle of good against evil uniting all faiths, recruiting Muslim-majority nations as partners.
option_explanations.C: Trump did not frame it as a purely military operation — his speech emphasizes partnerships, diplomacy, and shared resolve alongside military action.
option_explanations.D: Trump did not frame it as a conflict only America can fight — the whole point of the Riyadh address was recruiting Arab and Muslim partners. Unilateralism is the opposite of his framing.

items.explanation: Trump escalated the air war against ISIL in Syria and Iraq, and U.S.-backed forces destroyed the Islamic State's territorial caliphate by 2019.
items.stem: The Trump administration took military action against terrorists in

option_explanations.A: Correct. Trump escalated the air war against ISIL in Syria and Iraq, and U.S.-backed forces destroyed the Islamic State's territorial caliphate by 2019.
option_explanations.B: Armenia saw no Trump-administration military action against terrorists — the U.S. campaign against ISIL was in Syria and Iraq, not the Caucasus.
option_explanations.C: Cuba saw no Trump military action — U.S. policy toward Cuba under Trump was sanctions and reversal of the Obama opening, not military strikes.
option_explanations.D: Kuwait saw no Trump military action against terrorists — the anti-ISIL campaign was centered on Syria and Iraq, not Kuwait.

items.explanation: From the Eisenhower Doctrine through arms sales to Saudi Arabia, Washington has long advanced its Middle East interests through regional partnerships rather than direct rule. Trump's Riyadh summit -- courting Arab capitals as partners against Iran and extremism, later yielding the Abraham Accords -- is the latest iteration of that standing method.
options: A. Withdrawing all American forces from the Middle East
B. Refusing to deal with authoritarian governments
C. Relying on regional partnerships to advance American interests
D. Placing the region under United Nations administration
items.stem: Trump's direct outreach to Arab leaders continued which longer-term American approach in the Middle East?
items.stimulus:
Questions 6–8 refer to the following excerpt (paraphrased).

In his 2017 address in Riyadh, President Trump pledged to strengthen old friendships and build new partnerships — urging Arab and Muslim leaders to join the United States in confronting Islamist extremism and isolating Iran.
—After President Donald Trump's speech, May 2017

option_explanations.A: Trump did not withdraw all American forces from the Middle East — he kept forces in Syria and Iraq and built up partnerships. Withdrawal was never the longer-term American approach.
option_explanations.B: Washington has long dealt with authoritarian governments in the Middle East — from the Shah to the Saudi monarchy. Refusing such dealings was never the American approach.
option_explanations.C: Correct. From the Eisenhower Doctrine through arms sales to Saudi Arabia, Washington has long advanced its Middle East interests through regional partnerships rather than direct rule. Trump's Riyadh summit — courting Arab capitals as partners against Iran and extremism, later yielding the Abraham Accords — is the latest iteration of that standing method.
option_explanations.D: The United States never placed the Middle East under UN administration — American policy worked through bilateral partnerships and alliances, not UN rule.
